items.title: May 28, 2024 Meeting
items.text: May 28, 2024 Meeting Due to a technical error, the approval of these minutes will be heard at the June 25, 2024 meeting

items.title: General Public Comment
items.text: General Public Comment Francisco DaCosta commented on a meeting he attended with the Controller’s Office. He continued to comment on how the Bayview and Hunter’s Point districts are being impacted. Mary Butterwick provided remote comment and requested for the SFPUC not to appeal the Water Board’s recent ruling, but work with state to increase flow standards. Peter Drekmeier provided remote comment on the role of the Commission and how it should properly direct the SFPUC. Cindy Charles commented on the increasing water and sewer rates and would like to know what could be done to control these increases. Unidentified caller provided remote comment and asked the Commission to reconsider the alternative water supply plan to improve flows and other conditions, including increasing the levels of salmon. Unidentified caller provided remote comment and asked to reevaluate design drought plan

items.title: Report on Recent San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Activities, Events and Announcements
items.text: Report on Recent San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Activities, Events and Announcements DGM Ron Flynn provided comments on SFPUC employee Oscar Miron and his untimely passing. President Paulson requested a moment of silence in memory of Oscar

items.title: Award Contract No. WW-726, Various Locations Sewer Replacement No. 15, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Michael O'Shaughnessy Construction, Inc., in the amount of $8,308,717 and with a duration of 510 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and five months), to replace/line existing sewers on specified streets in the City and County of San Francisco. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. (Robinson)

Award Contract Nos. PRO.0266 A and B, As-Needed Research, Advertising, Community Engagement and Event Planning, to Most Likely To, Inc. (PRO.0266.A) and InterEthnica, Inc. (PRO.0266.B), each for an amount not-to-exceed $1,900,000 and a duration of four years. (Ordikhani)

Approve Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. PRO.0181, Westside Pump Station Construction Management Staff Augmentation Services, with MCK Americas, Inc., extending the contract duration by one year and six months for a new total contract duration of four years and six months, with no change to the contract amount, to continue construction management support for construction under Contract No. WW-645R, Westside Pump Station Reliability Improvements. (Robinson)

Approve Amendment No. 1 to the Memorandum of Agreement (Agreement) with the City of San Bruno regarding reimbursement of planning, design, and engineering costs for the provision of an additional one million gallons of emergency water storage in San Bruno Pressure Zone 1/4 at the Cunningham Tank site, as part of the operation of the Regional Groundwater Storage and Recovery Project. This Amendment No. 1 would retroactively extend the Agreement duration by 12 months, for a new total duration of 36 months, with no change to the Agreement’s not-to-exceed amount for the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission or San Bruno. (Ritchie) No Commission comment or public/remote comment. On the Motion to approve Item #6 – Consent Calendar:
Award Contract No. WW-742, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant 040/041/043 Health & Safety Improvements
items.text: Award Contract No. WW-742, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant 040/041/043 Health & Safety Improvements, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Anvil Builders, Inc., in the amount of $18,700,490, and with a duration of 940 consecutive calendar days (approximately two years and seven months), to provide health and safety improvements addressing structural, mechanical, instrumentation, controls, and electrical reliability, to the Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant wet weather primary sedimentation buildings. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. (Robinson) No Commission comment or public/remote comment. On the Motion to approve Item #7:

CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL regarding existing litigation
items.text: CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL regarding existing litigation (Government Code §54956.9, Administrative Code §67.10(d)(1)). RES System 3, LLC v. City and County of San Francisco Public Utilities Commission [Alameda County Superior Court Case No. 23CV037877, Filed September 26, 2022] Proposed settlement of a construction contract claim by RES System 3, LLC under DB-127, Warnerville Substation Rehabilitation Project. Material terms: SFPUC will pay nothing on Contractor’s claim; the SFPUC will release $2.6 million of the withheld contract balance; and the SFPUC will retain the remaining contract balance of $2,991,223. Proposed settlement subject to final approval by the Board of Supervisors. (Action Item) (Bregman) The Commission exited Closed Session at 4:16pm
